name: modal-dialog
description: Create a reusable modal dialog component

promptLevels.beginner: make a Modal class that can show and hide a dialog box
promptLevels.intermediate: create a Modal class with open and close methods, plus optional callback functions
promptLevels.advanced: write a Modal class that can be instantiated with options (title, content, callback functions), has open() and close() methods, and calls the appropriate callback when buttons are clicked
promptLevels.expert: Write a Modal class for creating reusable dialog boxes. The class should: 1) Accept an options object in the constructor with properties: title (string, optional), content (string or HTML, optional), onConfirm (callback function, optional), onCancel (callback function, optional). 2) Have an open() method that displays the modal. 3) Have a close() method that hides the modal. 4) Store whether the modal is currently open/closed as internal state. 5) Support calling onConfirm when a confirm action occurs and onCancel when a cancel action occurs. The class should allow multiple modal instances to be created with different configurations. The modal should maintain its own state and handle showing/hiding properly. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with an interface for ModalOptions defining the optional properties (title, content, onConfirm, onCancel). The class should have proper type annotations for all methods and properties. The callback types should be () => void. Store isOpen as a private boolean property. Export both the interface and the class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Create a Modal class with a constructor that accepts and stores the options object. Initialize isOpen to false. Implement open() and close() methods that update isOpen and call the appropriate callbacks. Export the class as default.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JSDoc with @typedef for ModalOptions object (with optional title, content, onConfirm, onCancel properties), @class for Modal, @property for isOpen, @param for the constructor options, and @returns void for methods. Document when callbacks are invoked. Export the class.

variants.typescript: Write a TypeScript Modal class that can show/hide and handle callbacks. Include proper interfaces for options.
variants.javascript: Write a JavaScript Modal class that can show/hide and handle callbacks.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript Modal class with JSDoc annotations that can show/hide and handle callbacks.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web:
Create a reusable modal dialog component in vanilla JavaScript. Include:

**HTML Structure:**
- Modal overlay (semi-transparent background)
- Modal container (centered box)
- Header with title and close button (X)
- Content area
- Footer with action buttons

**CSS:**
- Overlay covers full screen
- Modal is centered (vertically and horizontally)
- Smooth fade-in/fade-out animation
- Close button styled
- Backdrop click closes modal
- Responsive design

**JavaScript:**
- Modal class or factory function
- Methods: open(), close(), setContent()
- Click outside to close
- ESC key to close
- Event listeners for buttons
- Clean up on close

**Example Usage:**
```javascript
const modal = new Modal({
  title: 'Confirm Action',
  content: 'Are you sure?',
  onConfirm: () => console.log('confirmed')
});
modal.open();
```

Return as a single HTML file demonstrating the modal.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web-jsdoc:
Create a reusable modal dialog with complete JSDoc documentation. Same requirements as javascript-vanilla-web, plus:

- @typedef for ModalOptions
- @typedef for ModalConfig
- Complete @param and @return documentation
- @class documentation for the Modal class
- Document all public methods

Return as a single HTML file.
variants.typescript-vanilla-web:
Create a reusable modal dialog using TypeScript and vanilla Web APIs. Include:

**TypeScript:**
- Interface for ModalOptions (title, content, buttons, callbacks)
- Modal class with proper typing
- Type-safe event handlers
- Generic content type support

**Features:**
- Open/close methods
- Keyboard support (ESC to close)
- Click outside to close
- Customizable buttons
- Callbacks for actions
- Animation support

**HTML/CSS:**
- Clean, modern design
- Proper overlay and centering
- Animations

Provide TypeScript source and HTML structure.
